title: Vocalnayno: Designing a Game-Based Intervention to Support Reading Development in Primary Schools
venue: Proceedings of the 6th European Conference on Games-Based Learning
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a practical problem in primary-school reading support: how to help pupils develop reading skills while also giving teachers and teaching assistants better information about individual progress. The author argues that paper-based reading records and informal support from volunteers can be inefficient and may not provide timely, detailed feedback about specific phonics or reading weaknesses.

To explore this problem, the paper proposes and prototypes Vocalnayno, a game-based reading intervention intended for use on a laptop or tablet. In the game, children read letters, words, and phonics aloud to power gameplay, and the system records performance as an assessment metric that can be shared with teachers and parents. The design is framed as a supplement to existing primary-school practice, particularly the work of teaching assistants and parent volunteers.

The population and context are primary-school pupils in the UK, but the paper does not report a classroom deployment or a controlled evaluation. Instead, it describes an action-research-inspired design process, informal consultations with teachers, teaching assistants, parents, and children, and a very small pilot test of the prototype. The main conclusion is that the idea is promising as a way to combine engagement with objective assessment, but the current prototype is not yet ready for classroom use and needs a more accurate voice-recognition component and further development.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI or speech-enabled educational system without a specific commercial/product name. In this paper, the discussed concept is a game-based reading assessment and support tool that uses voice recognition to evaluate children reading letters/words aloud and provide feedback to teachers/assistants.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a design/prototype paper proposing 'Vocalnayno' as a game-based intervention for primary school reading development and assessment. It was not evaluated in a classroom trial; the author reports only informal discussions and a very limited pilot test of the prototype's voice recognition with the author and one primary school pupil.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/design-oriented paper with no classroom deployment and no empirical evaluation of reading outcomes. The only testing mentioned is a prototype pilot focused on voice recognition functionality, not literacy impact.
impact_tier_rationale: No outcome effects on reading or literacy are reported, so there is no demonstrated educational impact. The paper proposes a tool and describes design considerations rather than measured results.
